quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: Which lane position helps prevent other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane discourages other drivers from trying to share your lane. It also helps drivers behind you see you clearly in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: Motorcyclists are usually most easily seen by other drivers when riding in which lane position?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: The center lane position places you in the driver's rearview mirror where they are most likely to see you. Be ready to change positions if traffic or conditions require it.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making sudden moves.
questions.explanation: Sudden changes in speed or direction can cause a skid on slippery surfaces. Accelerate, shift gears, turn, and brake smoothly.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance if:

options.text: You believe stopping will be routine.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pavement is slippery.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when the pavement is slippery because your motorcycle will need more space to stop. Also increase it if you cannot see ahead clearly or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: When entering a curve, position your motorcycle:

options.text: On the outside of the curve.
On the inside of the curve.
Where you can most safely handle road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can most safely handle road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that fits the conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: How do convex mirrors differ from regular mirrors?

options.text: They provide a narrower view of the road.
They provide a wider view of the road.
They provide a clearer view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They provide a wider view of the road.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, vehicles in convex mirrors appear farther away than they actually are.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should generally be:
questions.correctAnswerText: In a staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets riders stay close while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file when taking curves, turning, entering highways, or exiting highways.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
Only stop to yield to other traffic.
Vehicles will be entering the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to all crossing traffic and pedestrians, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, how should the following distance change?
questions.correctAnswerText: Increase
questions.explanation: When towing a trailer, increase your following distance. The trailer adds weight, so your motorcycle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign with white background and red and black markings. It tells drivers that U-turns are not allowed in this area.

questions.question: What is required about footrests on a motorcycle?

options.text: The driver and passenger can share them
They are required for both the driver and passenger

questions.correctAnswerText: They are required for both the driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Motorcycles must have footrests for both the driver and passenger. Firm footing keeps your passenger from falling and pulling you off the bike too.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better
Ignore the stop line and move forward to get a better view
Stop at the stop line and then go through the intersection

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better
questions.explanation: First, stop at the stop line or stop sign. Then carefully move forward and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to check for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while you look.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder
Check your mirrors. You only need to look over your shoulder if you see something unusual
Either check your mirrors or look over your shoulder

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, make sure no vehicles are in your path. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.question: Where is the biggest danger of a crash between you and other vehicles?
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections are where crashes between motorcycles and other vehicles happen most often. The biggest danger is a car turning left in front of you.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, what is the minimum following distance for a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds
questions.explanation: Keep at least a two-second distance behind the vehicle in front of you under normal conditions. When conditions are not perfect, increase this distance.

questions.question: When making a normal stop on a motorcycle, which brakes should you use?

options.text: Both the front and rear brakes at the same time

questions.correctAnswerText: Both the front and rear brakes at the same time
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, apply the front and rear brakes at the same time and downshift.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to ride directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: The other vehicle may block your escape route
Other drivers can see you easily

questions.correctAnswerText: The other vehicle may block your escape route
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous because it could veer into your lane and hit you. It can also block your way to escape if a hazard appears.

questions.question: When turning, where should you look?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn
Turn just your head to look through the turn
Keep your knees away from the gas tank

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head to look through the turn
questions.explanation: Look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon. Keep your knees close to the gas tank to help with balance.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Use the rear brake before the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use the front and rear brakes at the same time when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, how does a motorcycle respond to braking and acceleration?

options.text: It takes less time to stop and speed up.
It takes the same amount of time to stop and speed up.
It takes more time to stop and speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes more time to stop and speed up.
questions.explanation: Extra weight slows down how fast a motorcycle can accelerate and decelerate. Your motorcycle will respond more slowly when you have a passenger than when you ride alone.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not necessary if you have a windshield.
It helps protect your whole face.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes, if you crash. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: When stopping, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. This lets you brake quickly and safely.

questions.question: When entering a turn, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed before you enter a turn. Taking a turn too fast can cause you to drift out of your lane or off the road.
